comparator.name: Liberal Arts and Sciences: Global Challenges
comparator.institution: Leiden University College The Hague, Leiden University
comparator.sourceNotes: The live 2026–27 Leiden product confirms a 180-EC degree: 45 EC first-year compulsory study, an 85-EC major, 10 EC electives, 30 EC minor/semester abroad/electives and 10 EC Global Citizenship. The generic target has six formal majors. CHS is selected before UCR fit as the broadest humanities-and-social-science expression of the generic interdisciplinary identity. The component list spans current CHS cultural-expression, historical-process and social-forms courses, its research-methods progression and 10-EC capstone; it selects Mathematics for Social Networks from the mathematics options and Spanish Beginners as a complete current Global Citizenship option. Genuine flexible space stays explicit. Every component is counted once and totals 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the generic degree, not one major. The official product lists six majors. CHS combines humanities and social sciences across culture, history, politics, society, difference and research and is the least narrowly disciplinary expression of the broad identity; it is selected before UCR course search.

core: Interdisciplinary analysis of global challenges and complex problems from multiple perspectives
Living together across cultures, histories and societies, with cross-cultural communication and global citizenship
Collective action, social difference, inequality, culture and the organisation of social life
Research design, qualitative and quantitative inquiry, data analysis and ethical reflection
Climate change, Earth systems, energy transitions, environmental sustainability and resource governance
Governance, economics, development and public institutions in addressing global problems
Human rights, international law and justice across borders
World politics, peace, conflict, security and international relations

questions: How can people respond to climate change and live together on a finite planet?
How do culture, historical power and social difference shape global citizenship and collective action?
How can institutions, law and international politics address inequality, conflict and development?

alternatives.label: Closest match to Global Challenges: Culture, History and Society
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines history, sociology, politics, philosophy, literature, media, communication and qualitative research, closely following the selected CHS route while retaining an interdisciplinary global-challenges identity.
alternatives.concept: An interdisciplinary humanities and social-science programme examining how cultures, histories, institutions and forms of social difference shape collective life and global challenges, with qualitative and historical research throughout.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort offerings were checked against the enriched workbook. PPD is in Year 1; foundations precede advanced theory, politics, media and research; all 24 courses are unique and eight are level 300.

alternatives.label: Earth Systems, Sustainability and Environmental Economics
alternatives.labelReason: Earth and environmental science, water, ecology, sustainability and resource governance dominate, with economics, data and quantitative methods supporting environmental decisions.
alternatives.concept: A science-and-policy route for understanding climate, Earth systems, biodiversity, water, energy and resource transitions, combining environmental research with economics, data analysis and sustainability governance.
alternatives.distinctness: Fourteen courses differ in each direction from the closest CHS programme. Earth and environmental gateways, GIS, hydrology, ecology, climate, resource science, economics and sustainability research replace much of the historical, literary, media and social-theory curriculum.
progression: Formal prerequisites and fixed cohort offerings were checked. Earth, sustainability, economics, mathematics and data foundations precede GIS, hydrology, resource analysis, upper-level research and governance; PPD is in Year 1 and eight courses are level 300.

alternatives.label: Global Politics, Justice and Political Economy
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum centres political theory, comparative politics, international relations, law, economics and security, with history, sociology, research and public communication as supporting disciplines.
alternatives.concept: A governance-centred route addressing global inequality, development, institutions, international law, human rights, conflict and political economy through political science, law, economics and social research.
alternatives.distinctness: Thirteen courses differ in each direction from CHS and twenty from Earth and Sustainability. Political economy, legal institutions, human rights and international security become the organising core.
progression: Formal prerequisites and fixed cohort offerings were checked. Gateways precede international, constitutional and EU law, public economics, econometrics, EU politics and peace and conflict. PPD is in Year 1 and eight courses are level 300.

candidates.label: Global governance, justice and world politics

selection.assessment: After the broad CHS response, two generator-backed formal directions pass coherence, feasibility and pairwise distinctness: Earth, Energy and Sustainability; and a governance cluster combining Governance, Economics and Development, International Justice and World Politics. All direct and stable interests are owned by the core or these candidates, and the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: Leiden embeds an 85-EC named major, prescribed research methods and a 10-EC capstone within a residential honours-college programme. UCR can assemble rigorous interdisciplinary 180-EC curricula, but these are illustrative compositions rather than official LUC majors and do not reproduce the residential structure or required capstone.
